fields.description:
## Problem
Nothing validates, before a reconcile pass mutates a live client Jira, that the mapped
projects actually EXIST / are visible to the bridge bot. Two live-only failure modes:
1. A mapped-but-nonexistent (or decommissioned / permission-lost) project key is
   syntactically valid, so `_validate_project_key` passes; the failure only surfaces
   deep in fan-out as an ACLI error. This is exactly the `05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27` incident class.
2. `resolve_project` (projects_store.py) returns `mapping.legacy_default` VERBATIM,
   unvalidated. Every unbound/legacy ticket (absent bridge_project) resolves there. The
   cross-project write guard's allowed set = `read_projects().keys()` and EXCLUDES creates
   (applier.py `_cross_project_targets`), so a legacy_default pointing at a real-but-wrong
   (or nonexistent) project drives a mass CREATE storm into the wrong place, unguarded.

## Approach
Add a reconcile-pass PREFLIGHT that runs BEFORE any outbound mutation and validates that
every project in `read_projects(repo_root).keys()` PLUS `legacy_default` (when set) is
visible to the configured backend. The probe reuses `access_check.py`'s existing
`AcliClient` transport (the same Jira Cloud transport `run_access_check` already drives) and
its retry helper (`_retry_sleep` / `JQL_RETRY_COUNT`). It enumerates the bot-visible project
keys through the client's ALREADY-PRESENT generic REST accessor
`AcliClient._direct_rest_get` (acli_rest.py:207 — the same helper used by
`get_issue_property`, `transition_issue`, and `validate_assignee_exists`) against the
standard Jira Cloud "Get projects paginated" endpoint `GET /rest/api/3/project/search`
(paginated via `startAt` with the response envelope's `values[].key` / `isLast`). No new
transport class or subprocess is introduced — only a new `access_check.py` helper consuming
the existing `_direct_rest_get` accessor.

Backend-neutrality: `access_check.py` is already Cloud/ACLI-specific, and this probe is a
Cloud-transport probe. To avoid breaking a Data Center-configured pass (whose pycontribs
transport exposes no `_direct_rest_get` / no `/rest/api/3` urllib path), the preflight
DEGRADES GRACEFULLY: when the configured client does not expose a callable `_direct_rest_get`
accessor, the preflight logs an observable "skipped: transport has no visible-projects probe"
message and returns without blocking the pass. It only enforces on the Cloud/ACLI transport
it is built for.

On a missing/invisible project (transport present, project absent from the visible set), FAIL
FAST with a clear, actionable message naming the offending key(s) and the fix (correct
projects.json / legacy_default), rather than letting fan-out crash mid-pass. A hard
auth/transport error (the probe cannot reach the backend) fails closed with its own distinct
"transport unavailable" message, kept separate from "project not visible". Wire it at the
reconcile pass entry (`__main__.py` `run_pass_result`, strictly before
`reconcile.reconcile_once`), skipping read-only passes (dry-run / reconcile-check / preview).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A pass with a mapped key not visible to the bot aborts at preflight with a clear
      message naming the offending key BEFORE any Jira write (no call to
      `reconcile.reconcile_once`). Verified by
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py -q`.
- [ ] `legacy_default` (when non-empty) is included in the preflight visibility check and an
      invisible `legacy_default` is caught, naming it. Verified by the same test module.
- [ ] An all-visible mapping passes preflight and the pass proceeds unchanged
      (`reconcile.reconcile_once` is called; no happy-path behavior change). Verified by the
      same test module.
- [ ] A hard auth/transport error fails closed with its own distinct message
      (transport-unavailable, not project-not-visible) and the preflight is observable via a
      log/stderr message. Verified by the same test module.
- [ ] A transport with no `_direct_rest_get` accessor (the Data Center backend shape) is not
      blocked: the preflight logs an observable skip and the pass proceeds. Verified by the
      same test module.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py -q` —
  fake/injected transport (no live Jira): a fake client whose `_direct_rest_get` returns a
  `project/search` page listing `{GOOD}` visible, `BAD` absent → preflight raises naming
  `BAD` and the pass makes no mutation; an all-visible mapping passes and the pass proceeds
  (`reconcile.reconcile_once` called); `legacy_default=WRONG` (not visible) is caught; a
  `_direct_rest_get` that raises fails closed with the transport-unavailable message; a fake
  client lacking `_direct_rest_get` is skipped (pass proceeds). RED first: without the
  preflight the pass proceeds to fan-out.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` from the worktree.

## Sequencing
Lives in `access_check.py` (new mapped-projects preflight helper consuming the existing
`_direct_rest_get` accessor) + wiring at the pass entrypoint (`__main__.py`
`run_pass_result`). Disjoint from A/B/C/E files. Reads projects_store (no edit).
